title: Fighting Heidelberg students in a Berlin beer room
summary: Locked in a room by dueling-scarred students, the Wooding men fought them off and the students had to be carried out.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: here. Why don't you get out?" "We don't have anything to do with that." So, they locked the door and Bobby Martin picked up his glass of beer to drink it and they dumped the glass of beer out of his hand. When they did that -- we had a fellow who was an ex-fighter, another dancer, Chick Horsey. George wasn't on the scene that night, he was out in the street somewhere. But Chick Horsey was even tougher than George. We had an English boy, a violinist named Boucher -- he weighed about 190, 6'2" -- there was Bobby Martin, myself and Herb Flemming. Well, when they knocked the beer out of Bobby's hand, we stood up and we started slugging. I just put my head down, man, but I got knocked down real quick. I didn't weigh but 140 pounds soaking wet then, so they knocked me down real fast. But those other four guys cleaned these students -- the students unlocked the door and got out. You know, they unlocked the door -- we didn't come out -- they unlocked the door to come out. And they had to carry them out. They laid them out, and Boucher got outside with his cane. He was born in England -- he was an English Negro, and as Chick Horsey would knock them and shove them out, Boucher would flatten them with the cane. And they had to carry them out. So, they threatened to bring the whole school back the next night, but they never showed up. That was one of the bad incidents of Berlin. We had another incident in Zurich, Switzerland. I'm always involved in these things. I don't know how I got mixed up -- always something
